body:
![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Creating a new `TextureLoader` and loading the same image for every enemy instance is highly inefficient and will lead to significant memory leaks, as textures are not being disposed. You should load the texture once and reuse it across all enemy sprites.

```suggestion
        const map = Enemy.texture || (Enemy.texture = new THREE.TextureLoader().load('assets/typhoon.png'));
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The tower type is currently hardcoded to `'gun'`, which means the player cannot place the 'Slow' or 'Heavy' towers even if they select them in the UI. This should use the selected tower type from the UI manager.

```suggestion
        const towerType = this.ui.selectedTower || 'gun';
```

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Instantiating a `TextureLoader` and loading the texture inside the `Enemy` constructor is highly inefficient. This triggers a new load operation and object allocation for every enemy spawned. You should load the texture once at the application level and reuse the material across all enemy instances.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Creating a new `SphereGeometry` and `MeshBasicMaterial` for every single projectile inside the update loop is a significant performance bottleneck. These Three.js objects should be instantiated once and reused across all projectiles to minimize memory allocation and garbage collection overhead.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The distance between waypoints is calculated every frame for every active enemy. Since the path is static, these segment distances should be pre-calculated once (e.g., in the `WaveManager` or when the path is defined) and stored to avoid redundant mathematical operations in the update loop.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The tower type is currently hardcoded to `'gun'`, which ignores the other tower types (Slow, Heavy) defined in the `CONFIG` and mentioned in the `README.md`. This logic should be updated to use the tower type selected by the player in the UI.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Using `alert()` is generally discouraged in games as it blocks the main execution thread and freezes the entire application. Consider implementing a non-blocking UI notification system to inform the player about insufficient funds.
